tasks.title: Write a program that inputs and validates pick weights; sorts PickedWeight[] and PickerName[] together from highest weight to lowest; outputs the top two names and weights as “Best in Group” and “Second best in Group”; stores names of members whose weight is over 3 kg in PickerCertificate[]; and outputs the number of certificates
tasks.prompt: Write a program that inputs and validates pick weights; sorts PickedWeight[] and PickerName[] together from highest weight to lowest; outputs the top two names and weights as “Best in Group” and “Second best in Group”; stores names of members whose weight is over 3 kg in PickerCertificate[]; and outputs the number of certificates. Use pseudocode or program code, comments and suitable input/output messages. Arrays and variables are already declared; PickerName[] is already filled.
tasks.model:
// GroupSize is the number of members
FOR Index ← 1 TO GroupSize
    REPEAT
        OUTPUT "Pick weight for ", PickerName[Index]
        INPUT PickedWeight[Index]
    UNTIL PickedWeight[Index] > 0
NEXT Index
// Keep each name with its weight while sorting
FOR Pass ← 1 TO GroupSize - 1
    FOR Index ← 1 TO GroupSize - Pass
        IF PickedWeight[Index] < PickedWeight[Index + 1] THEN
            TempWeight ← PickedWeight[Index]
            PickedWeight[Index] ← PickedWeight[Index + 1]
            PickedWeight[Index + 1] ← TempWeight
            TempName ← PickerName[Index]
            PickerName[Index] ← PickerName[Index + 1]
            PickerName[Index + 1] ← TempName
        ENDIF
    NEXT Index
NEXT Pass
OUTPUT "Best in Group: ", PickerName[1], PickedWeight[1]
OUTPUT "Second best in Group: ", PickerName[2], PickedWeight[2]
Count ← 0
FOR Index ← 1 TO GroupSize
    IF PickedWeight[Index] > 3 THEN
        Count ← Count + 1
        PickerCertificate[Count] ← PickerName[Index]
    ENDIF
NEXT Index
OUTPUT "Certificates to print: ", Count
tasks.context: Members of a litter picking group record their monthly pick. PickerName[] holds the names and PickedWeight[] holds weights in kg to one decimal place, such as 8.4. Matching indexes refer to the same member. The two heaviest picks win prizes. Every pick over 3 kg earns a certificate.

tasks.title: Write a program to find and output the maximum, minimum and average temperature for each day, including the day’s name
tasks.prompt: Write a program to find and output the maximum, minimum and average temperature for each day, including the day’s name. Then find and output the maximum, minimum and average for the whole week. Round every output temperature to two decimal places. Use pseudocode or program code with comments and suitable messages. Arrays and variables are already declared and Temperatures[] already contains the data.
tasks.model:
// Hours are rows 1..24; days are columns 1..7
MaxWeek ← Temperatures[1,1]
MinWeek ← Temperatures[1,1]
WeekTotal ← 0
DayName ← ["Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday"]
FOR Day ← 1 TO 7
    MaxDay ← Temperatures[1,Day]
    MinDay ← Temperatures[1,Day]
    DayTotal ← 0
    FOR Hour ← 1 TO 24
        Value ← Temperatures[Hour,Day]
        DayTotal ← DayTotal + Value
        IF Value > MaxDay THEN MaxDay ← Value ENDIF
        IF Value < MinDay THEN MinDay ← Value ENDIF
    NEXT Hour
    AvDay ← DayTotal / 24
    OUTPUT DayName[Day], " Maximum: ", ROUND(MaxDay,2), " Minimum: ", ROUND(MinDay,2), " Average: ", ROUND(AvDay,2)
    IF MaxDay > MaxWeek THEN MaxWeek ← MaxDay ENDIF
    IF MinDay < MinWeek THEN MinWeek ← MinDay ENDIF
    WeekTotal ← WeekTotal + DayTotal
NEXT Day
AvWeek ← WeekTotal / 168
OUTPUT "Week maximum: ", ROUND(MaxWeek,2), " minimum: ", ROUND(MinWeek,2), " average: ", ROUND(AvWeek,2)
tasks.context: A weather station records temperature hourly for a week. Temperatures[] is a 2D array with seven columns, Monday to Sunday, and 24 readings per column from 00:00 to 23:00. MaxDay, MinDay and AvDay hold daily results; MaxWeek, MinWeek and AvWeek hold weekly results.

scenario.title: Pre-release scenario · journey booking
scenario.text: A passenger travels home → start station → end station → destination. Each stage has a code and price. Add the three prices for the full journey. A start time after 10:00 earns a 40% discount. Task 1: set up arrays for stage codes/prices, passenger accounts (unique number and name), and bookings (passenger number, start time, three stage codes and unique booking number); store the stage prices. Task 2: let passengers open accounts with generated unique numbers, check account numbers when booking, generate a unique booking number and store the journey’s undiscounted price and details. Task 3: apply the time discount, display the price and booking details, then let the passenger confirm or start again. Validate entries, use meaningful names and clear prompts/messages.

tasks.model:

PriceStage1: REAL, stores matching prices, e.g. 1.50.
Equivalent arrays store the other stages, passenger accounts and bookings.

tasks.title: Write the Task 3 algorithm using pseudocode or programming statements
tasks.prompt: Write the Task 3 algorithm using pseudocode or programming statements. Assume Tasks 1 and 2 are complete.
tasks.model:
IF StartTime > "10:00" THEN
    TotalPrice ← TotalPrice * 0.60
ENDIF
OUTPUT "Journey price: ", TotalPrice
OUTPUT "Booking details: ", PassengerID, StartTime, StartCode, MiddleCode, EndCode, BookingID
OUTPUT "Are these details correct? Y/N"
INPUT Confirm
WHILE Confirm <> "Y"
    // Repeat the booking-entry process, including validation and price calculation
    CALL EnterJourney
    IF StartTime > "10:00" THEN TotalPrice ← TotalPrice * 0.60 ENDIF
    OUTPUT "Journey price: ", TotalPrice
    OUTPUT "Booking details: ", PassengerID, StartTime, StartCode, MiddleCode, EndCode, BookingID
    OUTPUT "Are these details correct? Y/N"
    INPUT Confirm
ENDWHILE

scenario.title: Pre-release scenario · computer shop
scenario.text: A customised computer starts with $200 of basic components. It must also include one case, one RAM option and one main hard disk. Other categories are optional, including the operating system. Task 1: store item codes, descriptions and prices in arrays; let the customer choose the three main items; calculate, store and output the selections and total. Task 2: let the customer add optional items, then store/output the extra selections and updated total. Task 3: give 5% off for exactly one additional item, or 10% off for two or more; output the saving and final price. Validate entries and use meaningful names, prompts and clear messages.

tasks.model: OneItemDiscount = 0.05 stores the fixed 5% rate for one additional item.

tasks.prompt: Explain the benefits of storing Price using a real data type.

tasks.title: Write the Task 1 algorithm
tasks.prompt: Write the Task 1 algorithm. You do not need to show array setup or initialisation. Use pseudocode or programming statements.
tasks.model:
// Arrays already contain the codes, descriptions and prices
REPEAT
    OUTPUT "Choose case code A1 or A2"
    INPUT CaseCode
UNTIL CaseCode = "A1" OR CaseCode = "A2"
REPEAT
    OUTPUT "Choose RAM code B1, B2 or B3"
    INPUT RAMCode
UNTIL RAMCode = "B1" OR RAMCode = "B2" OR RAMCode = "B3"
REPEAT
    OUTPUT "Choose main disk code C1, C2 or C3"
    INPUT DiskCode
UNTIL DiskCode = "C1" OR DiskCode = "C2" OR DiskCode = "C3"
// Look up each chosen item in the supplied arrays
FOR Index ← 1 TO 17
    IF ComponentCode[Index] = CaseCode THEN CaseIndex ← Index ENDIF
    IF ComponentCode[Index] = RAMCode THEN RAMIndex ← Index ENDIF
    IF ComponentCode[Index] = DiskCode THEN DiskIndex ← Index ENDIF
NEXT Index
TotalPrice ← 200 + ComponentPrice[CaseIndex] + ComponentPrice[RAMIndex] + ComponentPrice[DiskIndex]
OUTPUT "Selected items: ", Description[CaseIndex], Description[RAMIndex], Description[DiskIndex]
OUTPUT "Computer price: $", TotalPrice

tasks.title: Complete the trace, starting with Num = [45, 56, 30, 12, 15], indexed from 0 to 4
tasks.prompt: Complete the trace, starting with Num = [45, 56, 30, 12, 15], indexed from 0 to 4.
tasks.model: First pass: Flag=0; Count=0 swaps 45 and 56, Store=45, Flag=1; Count=1 and 2 make no swap; Count=3 swaps 12 and 15, Store=12. The array is now [56,45,30,15,12]. Second pass: Flag=0; Count=0,1,2,3 make no swaps; stop. Store stays 12.
tasks.code:
REPEAT
    Flag ← 0
    FOR Count ← 0 TO 3
        IF Num[Count] < Num[Count + 1]
        THEN
            Store ← Num[Count]
            Num[Count] ← Num[Count + 1]
            Num[Count + 1] ← Store
            Flag ← 1
        ENDIF
    NEXT Count
UNTIL Flag = 0

            Store ← Num[Count]
            Num[Count] ← Num[Count + 1]
            Num[Count + 1] ← Store
            Flag ← 1
        ENDIF
    NEXT Count
UNTIL Flag = 0
